items.title: Front seat-belt buckle release buttons can break (Montero)
items.summary: Red 'PRESS' release buttons can break, and the pieces can stop the buckle working properly.

items.title: Front seat-belt buckle release buttons can break (Dodge Raider)
items.summary: Same buckle problem on the Raider, under Chrysler's campaign.

items.title: Throttle valve icing (Montero)
items.summary: The throttle valve can ice up under certain conditions.

items.title: Throttle blade icing (Dodge Raider)
items.summary: The throttle blade can ice during extended highway driving below 10 °F.

items.title: Oil-pressure sender can leak
items.summary: The oil-pressure sending unit on the right side of the engine can leak oil, risking engine damage.

items.title: Aftermarket Reese trailer hitch weld (equipment)
items.summary: The receiver weld on a Reese hitch can break. This is an equipment recall, not a Mitsubishi or Chrysler campaign.

timeline.change: On sale in Japan in May: short-wheelbase three-door with a metal or canvas top. Petrol and diesel fours, part-time 4WD, torsion-bar IFS
Five-door long wheelbase arrives (February) and the high roof follows (July). Paris–Dakar debut in January: class win and 11th overall for Andrew Cowan
Uprated turbo-diesels. Cowan third overall on the Dakar in a modified-class Pajero
Four-speed automatic added (April). Zaniroli and Da Silva win the Paris–Dakar overall in a works prototype. LWB models get four-wheel discs and adjustable shocks
Exceed flagship (September). Dodge Raider (three-door) goes on sale in the US
3.0 6G72 V6 and an intercooled 2.5 turbo-diesel. LWB trucks switch to three-link coil rear suspension. Raider V6 (US)
Replaced by the second generation in January. Final US model year for the first-generation Montero (RS and LS)

identify.intro: Short or long, leaf or coil, four or V6, Mitsubishi or Dodge: the first generation comes in many combinations, and grey-import diesels add more.

items.head: Chassis codes
items.body: Mitsubishi's steering notice lists the first-generation codes: L041G, L043G, L044G, L046G, L048G, L049G, L141G, L144G, L146G and L149G.

items.head: Raider or Montero
items.body: The Raider is a Dodge-badged three-door only. A 'V6' grille badge marks the 3.0 V6 Raider. Mechanically it's the same as a three-door Montero.

items.head: Engine
items.body: US trucks have the 2.6 G54B SOHC four (109 hp) or the 3.0 6G72 V6 (143 hp). A diesel in the US is a later import.

items.head: Rear suspension
items.body: Leaf springs until 1988; LWB trucks then got three-link coils. BaT's 1988 Montero Sport short wheelbase still runs leaves.

items.head: Camel Trophy Edition
items.body: About 150 yellow short-wheelbase Camel Trophy Editions were built with the 4D56. Wikipedia says originals carry a yellow-and-black plaque and their own chassis code, and that replicas exist.

capability.v: Up to 7 in the LWB with the folding third row

values.intro: First-generation trucks are still cheap. Clean, original V6 LS Monteros and low-mileage Raiders are the ones that are going up.
values.note: Based on Bring a Trailer sold results since 2020. US Monteros and Raiders sold for $3,850 (a 1988 Montero Sport) to $24,000 (a 1990 Montero LS in May 2024); Raiders since 2024 went for $5,100–11,300. Imported Pajeros sold for about $3,850–16,250, and a 36k-mile 1988 Paris-Dakar Special brought $22,750 in 2018.

paragraphs: NHTSA's import exemption covers vehicles at least 25 years old, counted from each vehicle's own manufacture date (49 CFR 591.5(i)). As of October 2026 that includes every first- and second-generation Pajero, so right-hand-drive Japanese-market trucks, the 2.5 and 2.8 turbo-diesels and the Pajero Evolution can all be imported. Bring a Trailer has sold dozens of them since 2016.

The EPA exemption is separate. It requires the vehicle to be at least 21 years old and in its original configuration, or fitted with an equivalent or newer EPA-certified engine and emissions system, so keep the import paperwork. State titling and emissions rules vary, and California is the hardest. Canada's threshold is 15 years, which doesn't make a truck legal to bring into the US.
